title: Host-DRAM-lite AI servers decode data shards directly on GPU
idea: IFR: AI-server host memory shrinks to almost nothing. Constraint: adding no new chips means adding no scarce elements, so delete host DRAM's jobs instead: compressed training shards go storage-to-GPU and are decoded by GPU kernels, and checkpoints stream GPU-to-NVMe directly, removing the staging buffers that justify 1-2 TB per node.
why: Host DRAM per AI node drops from ~2 TB to ~256 GB, an 8x cut on a large slice of server DRAM bought today.
note: GPUDirect Storage and GPU decode already exist.

title: Utility meters, not itemized bills: fixed-size recurrent state in SRAM
idea: Borrowed from utility meters that keep a running total instead of every transaction: most attention layers are replaced by fixed-size recurrent/state-space states (a few MB per sequence) held in SRAM, plus a few exact-attention layers over a short local window.
why: Removes the linearly growing KV cache from DRAM; per-sequence memory becomes constant and fits on-die, so refresh power is zero.
note: Removes growing KV; known hybrids (Jamba, Samba); long-range recall without global attention is the doubt.

title: Minify resident chat sessions with typing-indicator KV prefetch
idea: Minify how long an LLM session's KV cache stays in HBM/DRAM: idle sessions are parked compressed in CXL flash. A restore is triggered by early client signals (tab focus, the typing indicator, a cursor in the input box), so the ~1-3 s it takes a human to type hides the reload.
why: Most conversations sit idle >90% of wall-clock time, so the resident KV footprint drops ~3-5x with no added latency the user can see.

title: Mycologist's spores: hibernate idle AI agents as compressed snapshots
idea: Fungi survive lean times as tiny spores. Agent sessions spend most of their wall-clock time waiting on users or tools. After ~2 s idle, the session's KV cache, runtime heap and sandbox are snapshotted into a compressed, deduplicated spore on NVMe and rehydrated in tens of ms by lazily paging in only the pages touched first.
why: Agent fleets keep thousands of mostly idle sessions resident. Spores cut resident DRAM/HBM per concurrent agent 10-20x.
note: Insight: agent sessions idle most of wall-clock time; snapshotting KV and heap to NVMe cuts resident memory per agent ~10x.

title: Gist tokens replace old context; raw chunks re-expand from flash
idea: Box: summarize × agent runtime × document chunk × leaves recent window × raw tokens on SSD. Older chunks are replaced by a few learned gist tokens' KV; if attention to a gist crosses a threshold the runtime re-prefills the original chunk from flash (zoom-in).
why: Million-token agents carry enormous KV; gist plus zoom keeps it ~20× smaller with recoverable fidelity.
note: Gist KV plus attention-triggered re-prefill could cut agent KV ~20x; doubt: gist fidelity and re-prefill latency spikes.

title: Typing-indicator KV prefetch for hibernated chat sessions
idea: When a response finishes, the server spills that session's KV cache to NVMe/CXL flash. It prefetches the cache back into HBM when the client sends a 'user started typing' or 'tab focused' event. This jumps from the nanosecond scale of HBM to the 5-60 s of human think time between turns, which hides a 10-200 ms restore completely.
why: HBM capacity and data movement (fact 5): live chat sessions are idle more than 90% of wall-clock time, yet their KV dominates inference HBM. Keeping only the actively decoding sessions resident cuts resident KV bytes about 5-15x.
note: KV offload known (LMCache, Mooncake); typing-signal prefetch is the twist.

title: Precision that ages: KV entries fade from FP16 to 2-bit
idea: Inverts 'a value keeps its precision for life': a background kernel demotes KV entries as they age or lose attention mass (FP16 to FP8 to INT4 to INT2), like a JPEG whose quality fades with distance, while recent and high-attention tokens stay sharp.
why: Average KV storage near 3 bits per element instead of 16: a 4-5x KV footprint cut at long context with small accuracy loss.
note: Importance/age-based KV precision (KIVI, MiKV, ZipCache) is crowded art.

title: Cobalt kobold miners: tiny SRAM index picks which KV pages to fetch
idea: Cobalt is named for the kobold that hunted ore; each 16-token KV page gets a 64-byte summary (per-channel key min/max) in SRAM, decode computes upper-bound attention scores from the summaries and fetches only the top 3-5% of pages from DRAM, while the rest of the KV lives in CXL memory or NAND.
why: Per-token KV traffic falls 20-30x (well over 10x lower energy per access), and the HBM/DRAM KV footprint shrinks to the hot pages with the long tail in cheaper flash (energy, cost/bit).

title: Swap fixed-precision KV for age-graded fading precision
idea: Substitute uniform precision with human-like memory decay. KV entries are written at 8 bits; a background kernel requantizes them to 4 bits after ~1k tokens and 2 bits after ~8k, then evicts them, unless their cumulative attention mass marks them salient. This is pure software on unchanged HBM.
why: Long contexts average about 3 bits per element instead of 16, a ~5x KV cut that keeps important tokens sharp.

title: Sourdough starter: persist tokens, regrow KV on demand
idea: Keep only the starter: persist each session's token IDs (2-4 bytes per token) to flash and drop its KV cache (100 KB+ per token on large models) under pressure; a cost model chooses between regrowing KV by prefill on idle compute and fetching a stored copy.
why: Persistent state shrinks ~10^4-10^5x per token; exploits compute being more abundant than memory.

title: Run cache-sized services on gigabyte-LLC CPUs with minimal DIMMs
idea: Box: substitute × existing large-L3 CPUs (~1 GB stacked SRAM) × whole working set × deployment time × minimal DIMM population. Routers, rate limiters, feature-flag and session services whose working sets fit in ~1 GB are pinned to large-cache parts already in the fleet, with one small DIMM per channel.
why: Those services get 256–512 GB per box by default; running them cache-resident frees 80–95% of their DRAM using installed silicon, so nothing new passes through fluorinated etch or PFAS lithography.

title: Roll-to-roll web: stream tiles depth-first through every layer
idea: Activations are treated like the web in a roll-to-roll line. Each input tile runs through all layers (or a deep stage) before the next tile enters, and the overlap 'splice' halos at tile edges are recomputed. Full feature maps are never written to DRAM; only a moving web of tiles stays in on-chip SRAM. The compiler picks tile size the way a line picks web width, trading halo recompute against buffer size.
why: Activation memory for vision, diffusion and video models falls 10-50x, and DRAM traffic for intermediate tensors (fact 5) mostly disappears, at a cost of about 5-15% extra compute.
